text:
Rafael Mendes: ok need to lock KPIs for the failover automation upgrade before next week’s steering sync. want something we can actually measure + report. goals we’ve been using: fewer incidents, faster detect/mitigate, fewer customer-impact mins, avoid unsafe failovers.

Talia Benson: +1. I’m putting together the program status template and I need the “headline metrics” + cadence (weekly vs monthly).

Aisha Bello: can we align the KPIs w/ the multi-region SLO + error budget view? otherwise we’ll be arguing about what “success” means in every retro.

Miles Thornton: for the trigger/orchestrator work specifically, we should have a KPI that captures “automation did the right thing” not just overall incidents (which can change due to other stuff).

Tomáš Novák: + also don’t forget runbook/on-call angle. time-to-detection and time-to-mitigation are the big levers vs “incident count” which is noisy.

Sergio Costa: I can pull data from incident timeline fields + our Grafana annotations once we standardize the event tags (failover_state_change, degrade_mode_on/off, etc).

Rafael Mendes: ok proposal draft (tell me what’s wrong):
1) Incident count by cause (regional routing/dns, upstream dep, capacity saturation, networking/packet loss, control plane) for customer-impacting incidents only.
2) MTTR for regional incidents (time from “incident declared” to “SLO burn back under threshold / customer impact resolved”).
3) Time-to-detection (TTD): first SLO burn alert fired -> incident declared.
4) Time-to-mitigation (TTM): incident declared -> first mitigating action applied (failover start, degrade mode enabled, load shed, etc).
5) Avoided failovers: # of times trigger engine recommended/entered degrade mode and we did NOT full-failover, and impact stayed within SLO.
6) False failovers / near-miss: any failover that later gets labeled “should not have happened”.

Aisha Bello: 👍 on 2-4, but define them tightly or we’ll get garbage. also (3) “first SLO burn alert fired” can be tricky because we have multiple alerts (5xx, p99, burn). we should choose a single canonical page.

Allison Grant: agree. recommend canonical = multi-window burn-rate for the multi-region availability SLO. we can still log supporting alerts but KPI should reference one.

Sergio Costa: ^ from the observability side easiest is: use alertname=mr_availability_burnrate (the one from slo-toolkit) as the “TTD start”. then TTD end = incident created in incident bot or PagerDuty.

Tomáš Novák: question on MTTR: do we care “resolved” vs “mitigated”? sometimes we fail over and things are stable but root cause investigation takes hours.

Rafael Mendes: good call. maybe split:
- Time-to-stabilize: incident declared -> customer impact below SLO thresholds for 30 min
- Time-to-resolve: incident declared -> incident closed
We report stabilize as the KPI; resolve for internal tracking.

Miles Thornton: for failover engine itself, can we track:
- Detection-to-action latency for automated path: trigger condition met -> orchestrator enters FAILOVER_PENDING -> traffic shift begins
and
- Automation coverage: % of eligible routes/models/tiers with automation enabled (or at least monitor-only)

Aisha Bello: coverage metric is key for the project phases. otherwise we’ll “succeed” with 1 route enabled.

Talia Benson: can we keep the exec-level KPIs to 4-5 bullets max, and we can have additional engineering metrics in the weekly update?

Neha Kapoor: popping in — yes please keep the exec dashboard crisp. I care most about: (a) customer impact mins from regional issues, (b) time to stabilize, (c) unsafe/flappy failovers = zero, and (d) rollout coverage trending up.

Rafael Mendes: got it. Let’s map.
Exec KPIs:
A) Customer impact minutes from regional impairment (proxy: error budget burn minutes for MR availability SLO + “degraded but available” minutes) — baseline vs after rollout.
B) Time-to-stabilize for regional incidents (median + p90).
C) Unsafe failovers (count) + flappy failovers (count).
D) Automation coverage (% traffic under monitor-only, % traffic under auto with guardrails).
E) Avoided failovers (count) w/ short notes (why we avoided + did degrade instead).

Aisha Bello: careful w/ “customer impact minutes” as error budget burn minutes — it’s the best standardized thing we have, but we should explicitly state it’s a proxy and link to the SLO doc.

Allison Grant: +1. Also: impact minutes should be scoped to routes included in the MR SLO. Dedicated has some different SLOs.

Miles Thornton: for “unsafe vs flappy” definitions:
- unsafe failover = failover executed when safe-to-failover checks were failing OR we exceeded stop conditions and didn’t auto-abort
- flappy = failover started then rolled back within hold-down window due to signal recovery (not operator-driven)
Does that match what we want?

Tomáš Novák: also include “manual override events” count? if we’re overriding constantly, automation isn’t doing the job.

Rafael Mendes: good. add sub-metric: Manual override actions (enable/disable auto, force failover, force rollback) w/ reason code. not exec KPI but in weekly.

Sergio Costa: data sources:
- incidents: incident-bot timeline + PD (if declared)
- SLO burn: slo-toolkit metrics
- failover states + overrides: orchestrator audit log events (we’re already emitting those)
- coverage: routing policy store + feature flag service (I can add a query)
I can wire a weekly export and a Grafana panel set.

incident-bot: Reminder: You can tag incidents with `cause=<cause>` and `impact=customer|internal` using `/incident update`.

Aisha Bello: tagging is the missing piece. if we want “incident count by cause”, we need a controlled taxonomy and enforce it in postmortems.

Tomáš Novák: we can add “cause” to the incident review checklist + make it required before closure.

Talia Benson: what’s the taxonomy list? keep it short.

Rafael Mendes: propose:
- regional_capacity
- regional_network
- regional_dependency (cloud provider / upstream auth / storage)
- regional_routing_dns
- control_plane
- unknown
And a “secondary” freeform field in the postmortem.

Aisha Bello: ok. also define what counts as “regional incident” for KPI rollups:
- any incident where impact is isolated primarily to a region OR mitigation involved cross-region traffic shift / degrade-mode for a region

Miles Thornton: + include “partial impairment” where we did load shed + fallback variants without full failover.

Rafael Mendes: yep.

Cadence proposal:
- Weekly (SRE + platform): post in #eng-sre every Monday: coverage, overrides, any failover/degrade events, KPI deltas + notes.
- Monthly (exec steering): 1 slide with the Exec KPIs above + 2-3 bullets on learnings/changes.
- After every controlled failover test: 48h readout using the post-test template (timeline, impact, alert behavior, gaps, action items).

Neha Kapoor: works for me. monthly is enough as long as the weekly is consistent and issues are escalated quickly.

Sergio Costa: I’ll take action to draft the dashboard + a simple weekly report query. who owns writing the “weekly Monday post”? Talia or SRE?

Talia Benson: I can own posting the template if someone drops the numbers in a doc by EOD Sunday. but realistically SRE should own the numbers.

Rafael Mendes: SRE will own. I’ll rotate it between me + Tomáš for now. once dashboards are stable we can automate the post.

Tomáš Novák: 👍

Aisha Bello: I’ll update the SLO page w/ KPI definitions + the canonical alertname for TTD. also will add “cause tagging required” note.

Miles Thornton: I’ll write up the definitions for unsafe/flappy + avoided failovers and stick them in the runbook/ADR appendix.

Rafael Mendes: cool. decision: lock exec KPIs A-E as above; weekly engineering KPIs include overrides + detection-to-action latency + incident count by cause. Talia will add cadence to the program overview. thanks all.

Sergio Costa: :thumbsup: I’ll share a draft Grafana link in this thread tomorrow.

Neha Kapoor: thanks — please also include a baseline period (last 90 days) so we can show trend vs “before automation”.

Rafael Mendes: yep, baseline = trailing 90d pre-flag enable (monitor-only) + annotate the prod test dates. will do.
